newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel Alsthom first-half loss narrows.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel Alsthom first-half loss narrows.

text.p: French telecommunications and engineering giant Alcatel Alsthom reported on Thursday its first half loss narrowed and said it was on track to break even this year and even show a profit including capital gains.

Chairman Serge Tchuruk said the sale of Alcatel's 25 percent stake in the Cofira mobile telephone company to British Telecommunications Plc would lead to a 1996 profit, including capital gains, of "several billion francs."
He also told a news conference the group maintained its expectation of a "good" profit by 1998.
Alcatel reported a net loss of some 400 million francs ($78.1 million) for the first half of 1996, compared with a loss of 1.2 billion francs for the year-earlier period.

It said the narrowing of the half-year loss was due mainly to a more favourable tax situation and was in line with its action plan. But it noted that the effects of a recovery plan introduced last year were still limited.
It said asset sales since 1995 totalled 4.9 billion francs, or about half of its 1996 disposal programme. ($ = 5.122 French Francs)
